payload.claim: A sampling of the spec's path:line citations in the Context and Notes-for-the-agent sections drift from the actual line numbers at this snapshot by roughly 1-30 lines, though each still lands in the right function/region with the described behavior confirmed accurate. Examples: `argued = {...}` in saffron/cell/session.py is actually at 3733-3737 (spec says 3730-3734); the record_rebuttal call site is at 3742-3746 (spec says 3738-3743); record_rebuttal's own definition in saffron/ledger.py is at 2160-2177 (spec says 2146-2162); `rebut_result: ... = None` binds at session.py:3421 and `blockers = review.anchored_blockers(reviews)` at 3434 (spec says 3418/3431); the two record_rebuttal calls in tests/test_ledger_fold_task.py's fixture are at lines 194 and 196 (spec says 193/195); and the pool-cut case "a" fixture the spec points to at tests/test_session.py:5360 is actually part of test_a_rebut_the_cap_cut_short_ends_exhausted_with_its_blockers_standing's cut_short list around line 5389-5398. By contrast, several other citations checked (saffron/phases/rebut.py:641-642, :663-664, saffron/task.py:1036-1037/1079-1080, saffron/phases/package.py:1070-1071, saffron/record/migrate.py:84, 87-93, 96-105, 534-545, and the prose-gate's ten-line docstring limit at saffron/phases/rebut.py:630-640) are exact. None of this changes which code the plan targets or how the witnesses must be built; it is citation imprecision an implementer would resolve by reading the named function, not a defect in the plan.
